reasoning: The question asks about ECB balance sheet changes over a single week (Oct 11 to Oct 18, 2026). The evidence shows the ECB raised rates to 2.50% in September 2026 and is expected to hold in October, with inflation concerns from Middle East energy shocks. Higher rates typically lead to balance sheet reduction as the ECB maintains restrictive policy. Historical ECB patterns since 2022 show gradual balance sheet reduction through quantitative tightening. With no evidence of new asset purchases and ongoing restrictive monetary policy, a weekly decrease is more likely than an increase.
